Documentation → Plugin Studio: build your own → Code-first scripts

Code-first scripts — one file, SATOM data, the developer kit

Write a script whose form, connections and settings live in main.py (the SATOM block), read SATOM's own data with satom.devices / lb_lookup / dns_lookup, try it on your computer with the developer kit, then import the file as an app in one step.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsstudio.script_library
📍 WherePlugin Studio → Apps → Import a script / Developer kit
On this page
  • Why
  • Step 1 — the SATOM block
  • Step 2 — read SATOM's data
  • Step 3 — try it on your computer
  • Step 4 — import it
  • Next

Why#

A script used to live in two places: the code, and its form and settings on the editor's tabs. Rename a field in one and not the other, and inputs["ip"] fails at run time. Code-first puts everything in main.py, so the file you read is the whole plugin — easy to see, copy and adapt.

📌Required

You need studio.script_library. The data calls satom.lb_lookup and satom.dns_lookup need network.view for the person who runs the script.

Step 1 — the SATOM block#

Start main.py with a SATOM = {...} block:

SATOM = {
    "id": "lb-members-owner",
    "name": "LB members and their owner",
    "inputs": {
        "query": {"label": "Name or address", "required": True},
        "ask_cmdb": {"label": "Ask the CMDB about each member", "type": "checkbox"},
    },
    "connections": ["cmdb"],
    "satom": ["lb_lookup", "dns_lookup"],
    "network": "none",
    "timeout": 120,
}

from satom_script import inputs, connection, satom, log, result
Key What it sets
inputs The form, in order: {"name": {"label", "type", "required", "default", "help", "options"}} — or just the label for a text field. Types as on the Form tab.
connections The connections connection("id") may call
satom The SATOM data the script reads (step 2)
network, timeout As on the Settings tab
credentials Names for secret("NAME")
name, description, id The app's name and description; id is used by Import a script

SATOM reads the block — it never runs it — so only literals are allowed (text, numbers, True/False/None, lists, dicts). When you save, the form and settings come from the code; the Form and Settings tabs show them read-only. Who can run it stays a setting in SATOM.

A mistake in the block shows as a problem with its line, like a syntax error: test runs and publishing wait until it is fixed, and the last good form stays. For an existing script, Form → Move the form into the code writes the block for you.

Step 2 — read SATOM's data#

lb = satom.lb_lookup(inputs["query"])          # virtual servers, pools, members
names = satom.dns_lookup(lb["members"])        # PTR names of the members
devices = satom.devices(product="fortiweb")    # the devices you may see
Call Answers
satom.devices(product="", zone="", line="", department="", maintenance="include") A list of devices: id, name, kind, version, host, ip, zone, line, department, maintenance
satom.lb_lookup(entries, exact=False) rows (one per match, with _members = [{ip, port, status}]), members, unmatched, gateways
satom.dns_lookup(entries, ttl=False) rows, answers, unresolved, ptr = [{ip, hostname}]

Each answers for the person who runs the script, in the ADOM they started it from — what the pages show them there. Nothing goes to a device and nothing writes. A call the script does not declare is refused, and a run without a person (a schedule with no owner) cannot read SATOM data. Give as many names as you need: SATOM answers 50 per call and satom_script splits a longer list into calls and joins the answers. Each call is a line in the run's log.

Step 3 — try it on your computer#

Plugin Studio → Apps → Developer kit downloads the SDK (the same file the jail runs), the block reader, a README and this example with canned answers:

python3 satom_script.py form example/main.py
python3 satom_script.py run example/main.py --input query=www.example.com \
    --input ask_cmdb=yes --mocks example/mocks.json

mocks.json answers satom.* and each connection ("GET /path", "GET *", "*", "sql"). Like SATOM, a local run refuses a connection or SATOM data that the block does not declare, and a required input you did not give.

Step 4 — import it#

Plugin Studio → Apps → Import a script, choose main.py (or a .zip with it). The app is created with the block's id, name and form; an id already in use is refused and nothing is overwritten. Test it on Test, then Publish.

The same example is in Plugin Studio → Examples → Code-first script: LB members and their owner (ex-lb-members-owner): it works at once on the LB cache; the CMDB part needs the ex-cmdb connection pointed at your CMDB.

Next#

  • Everything else a script can do: Script Library.
  • Build and test plugins away from production: SATOM Builder.
